entities.name: Antón de Alaminos
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Antón de Alaminos, born in Palos de la Frontera in 1482, emerged as the preeminent Spanish marine pilot of the early sixteenth century, whose unparalleled expertise in New World navigation proved instrumental in the foundational phase of Spanish colonization. Having sailed with Christopher Columbus on his second voyage in 1493, Alaminos acquired firsthand experience with transatlantic crossings, laying the groundwork for his later pivotal roles. His profound understanding of ocean currents and winds, particularly the Gulf Stream, made him an indispensable asset to major expeditions, fundamentally shaping the geographic and economic contours of the burgeoning Spanish Empire.

Alaminos's career is marked by participation in several epoch-making voyages. In 1513, he served as chief pilot for Juan Ponce de León's expedition that led to the European discovery of Florida. Five years later, in 1518, he guided Juan de Grijalva's fleet along the Yucatán Peninsula, providing crucial reconnaissance of the Mexican coast. Perhaps most famously, in 1519, Alaminos piloted Hernán Cortés's invasion fleet from Cuba to the coast of Mexico, ensuring the successful landing that initiated the Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire. His most significant contribution, however, was the systematic discovery and utilization of the Gulf Stream for the return journey to Spain, dramatically shortening the voyage and making regular transatlantic communication feasible.
